stories.headline: Spain's transport minister refuses to resign over high-speed rail disaster
stories.summary: Facing calls to step down after Wednesday's deadly high-speed train collision in Toledo province, Spain's transport minister said he will stay on as investigators examine the crash.

stories.summary: Shelby Vaughn scored in the 88th minute off a run by Renee Watson as the Spartans closed the Big Ten regular season with a road win.

fear_greed.commentary: The index slid deeper into fear at 26, down from 35 at the prior close and below 30 a month ago, though still above the extreme-fear reading near 17 a week ago.

markets.summary: October ended with a broad tech-led rout as disappointing results from Intel and Amazon, on top of Alphabet's record one-day drop Thursday, deepened worries about the payoff from heavy AI spending: the Nasdaq fell 2.86% to 25,437.00, the S&P 500 1.82% to 7,580.07 and the Dow 1.09% to 51,770.31, leaving the Nasdaq down about 5% for the month, its worst since March 2025. Chips led the losses, with Intel down about 29% on weak guidance and Nvidia off 4.2% to $204.64, now barely above its 40-week average with RSI near 35 and MACD below its signal line. Small caps held up better, as the Russell 2000 slipped 1.66% to 2,811.84 but stayed up 1.3% on the week and above its 40-week average. The 10-year Treasury yield eased to about 4.93%. Metals sold off hard: gold futures fell 3.3% to $3,898.90 and silver futures 5.9% to $49.10, both well below their 40-week averages, with silver down 18% over the past month and its RSI near 22, deep in oversold territory.

stories.headline: SpaceX slides as Anthropic named its largest customer
stories.summary: Bloomberg reported that Anthropic is the unnamed customer behind about 34.5% of SpaceX's third-quarter revenue under compute contracts that can be cancelled with notice from early 2027, adding concentration worries to the tech sell-off; SPCX closed down 6.4% at $134.72.

stories.headline: SpaceX stock drops on launch setback and sector selloff
stories.summary: StreetInsider also cited a reported launch setback, Bank of America flagging China as the main regulatory hurdle to any SpaceX-Tesla merger, and continued post-IPO lockup selling.

stories.headline: Cameco tumbles after Q3 adjusted loss
stories.summary: Cameco posted a C$2 million adjusted net loss on C$619 million in revenue as a planned Key Lake mill outage cut production 20% and raised costs, and it narrowed 2026 guidance; CCJ closed down 7.9% at $76.91.

stories.headline: Cameco reports 2026 third quarter results
stories.summary: The company's release reports C$43 million in net earnings, C$860 million in cash, and a 2026 annual dividend of C$0.24 per share payable Dec. 15.

stories.headline: Why Nvidia stock took a dive today
stories.summary: Beyond the chip sell-off, Bloomberg reported Nvidia is in talks to provide billions in credit guarantees for an Nscale data center to be used by Anthropic, renewing worries about circular AI financing; Nvidia reports earnings Nov. 17.

headlines.headline: Intel posts worst day since the 1970s as Amazon also slides on AI spending worries
headlines.summary: Intel plunged 29% on weaker-than-expected guidance and Amazon fell after an earnings miss, pulling chip stocks and the Nasdaq sharply lower.

weather.summary: A wet Halloween weekend for the Southwest: a first wave of heavy rain moves through the Four Corners into Saturday morning, then a second, wider round reaches southern California Saturday evening and spreads into the Great Basin and Four Corners Sunday, heaviest along Arizona's Mogollon Rim. Rain and storms also shift from the southern Plains toward the Gulf Coast, while high pressure keeps most of the East dry, colder than normal in New England and milder to the south.
